feedback: The geometry with a slightly narrower sensor spread of ±0.04 m and sensor size 0.016 m helps reduce sensor noise and improves control stability, especially in tight curves like the s-bend. The integrator had to compensate for the previous wider sensor spread noise by tuning the controller gains and reducing base speed. The narrower spread should reduce noise further and improve line detection consistency. The integral gain increase aims to reduce steady-state error in curves, while the slight speed reduction balances control and progress. The sensor positions remain symmetric and close to the axle to maintain stable sensing. The line loss strategy remains 'search_left' to steer right on loss, which worked well previously. Requested changes: 1) Test sensor_positions spread at ±0.035 m to further reduce noise and improve stability. 2) Try increasing ki to 1.2 to enhance integral correction if steady-state error persists. 3) Experiment with base_speed at 1.0 to see if slower speed improves control on the s-bend without sacrificing too much progress.
